# Pane

> Pane (current version 1.0.0) is a free, open source macOS menu bar app for window snapping with the trackpad. Swipe two fingers on the active window's title bar to snap it to a half, a quarter or the full screen. It runs on macOS 13 Ventura or later, on Apple silicon and Intel Macs.

## Gestures

- Swipe left or right on the title bar: left or right half of the screen.
- Swipe up: fill the screen. Swipe down: minimize.
- Swipe diagonally: one of the four quarters.
- Swipe toward an edge the window already fills: move it to the next monitor. On a single screen, the same swipe again goes from a half to two thirds to one third.
- A light haptic click in the trackpad when the preview jumps to a new layout (can be turned off).
- A Settings window: swipe length, preview, haptics, the Option mode, launch at login and the Accessibility status.
- Hold Option to swipe anywhere on screen; it always moves the active window.
- A blurred preview shows where the window will land; swipe back to cancel. Scrolling everywhere else is left alone.

## Is it safe?

- Open source under the MIT License, written natively in Swift.
- No analytics, no account. The only network request is a version check when the user clicks Check for updates.
- It needs the Accessibility permission, which macOS requires for any app that reads and moves other apps' windows.
- Distributed as a DMG (and a zip). Each release lists SHA-256 checksums.
- Not notarized by Apple yet: on first launch, open it once, then System Settings > Privacy & Security > Open Anyway.

## Price

- Free. It is a free, open source alternative to paid trackpad window managers such as Swish.
